The atmosphere at The Den was electric on May 2, 2026 , as Millwall hosted Oxford United in a Championship clash with significant implications for both sides. Supporters gathered in anticipation of a high-stakes encounter where every individual duel and tactical adjustment promised to shape the final narrative of the season. First Half Breakthrough The match began with a high tempo as both sides looked to establish early dominance in the midfield. However, the rhythm was disrupted early for the visitors when Yunus Emre Konak was forced off the pitch just 16 minutes into the contest. He was replaced by Cameron Brannagan , a change that forced Oxford United to recalibrate their engine room sooner than expected. Despite the early disruption, the game remained a cagey affair until the 34th minute, when the deadlock was finally broken. A precise passage of play saw Mihailo Ivanovic provide a clever assist to find Femi Azeez , who made no mistake in front of goal to send the home support into raptures. As the first half drew toward its conclusion, the physical intensity of the Championship was on full display. Thierno Ballo found his name in the referee's book in the 39th minute, receiving a yellow card for a mistimed challenge as Oxford United struggled to contain the mounting pressure from the hosts. The referee eventually blew for the interval after five minutes of added time, leaving the visitors with plenty of work to do to find a way back into the game. Azeez Strikes Again Millwall wasted no time asserting their authority in the second half. Just three minutes after the restart, Femi Azeez proved to be the protagonist once again. In the 48th minute, the clinical forward found himself in the right place at the right time to double the advantage, effectively shifting the momentum entirely in favor of the South London side. The brace showcased Azeez 's predatory instincts and left the Oxford United defense searching for answers as the deficit widened. Faced with a two-goal mountain to climb, both managers turned to their benches near the hour mark to inject fresh energy into the contest. Oxford United made a triple substitution, introducing Mark Harris , Jin-Woo Jeon , and Jamie McDonnell in place of Will Lankshear , Stanley Mills , and Jamie Donley . Millwall responded shortly after with changes of their own, bringing on Billy Mitchell and Alfie Doughty for Casper de Norre and Zak Sturge . The flurry of activity continued as Thierno Ballo made way for Luke Cundle , as the game entered a frantic tactical phase. Late Tactical Chess With the lead comfortably in hand, Millwall focused on game management and defensive solidity throughout the final quarter of the match. The man of the hour, Femi Azeez , was withdrawn in the 73rd minute to a standing ovation, replaced by William Smallbone to shore up the midfield. The visitors continued to push for a lifeline, but the home defense remained resolute, frustrating every attempt to breach their lines. Further substitutions followed as Barry Bannan was replaced by Macaulay Langstaff for the hosts, and Sam Long came on for Hidde ter Avest in the closing stages. As the clock ticked deep into stoppage time, the referee finally brought the proceedings to a close after five minutes of additional play. It was a professional and disciplined performance from Millwall , who utilized the clinical finishing of Azeez to secure all three points. For Oxford United , the afternoon served as a difficult reminder of the fine margins at this level, as they were unable to recover from the double blow dealt by the hosts' star man.
